claims.claim: Color appearance depends on surround, adaptation and viewing conditions
Luminance structure is generally more robust than hue-only structure for legibility
Hue-temperature mapping is a direct universal sensory axis
Hue-temperature associations are measurable but moderated
Cone opponency and chromatic adaptation contribute to complement/afterimage effects
One complementary wheel predicts neutralization, discrimination and harmony
Simultaneous contrast is robust and mechanism-plural
Induction can reverse toward assimilation with geometry and spatial frequency
Chroma/colorfulness depend on luminance, surround, gamut and adaptation
Increasing saturation generally resolves CVD discrimination
Fixed color-area ratios universally predict perceptual balance
Salience depends on multiscale feature competition and task
HDR/OLED appearance is determined by class label alone
Accessibility requires redundant encoding and rendered-state validation
